_readme: Facts that must have exactly ONE definition, and must have it in a named file.
This is not the same thing as the count ratchet. A ratchet says 'do not add a 37th'; this says
'there is exactly one, and it lives HERE'. It therefore also catches a definition that MOVED,
and it names the surviving home in the refusal so the fix is obvious.
checks.sh rule 9c already refuses two functions with the same NAME. Nothing here duplicates that:
these are values and call shapes, which rule 9c cannot see.
Phases 3 and 4 of the refactor programme add a line here per consolidation -- unit constants, the
day-label array, the metric_type enum, fmtDateGB, _isSolo, the 1RM entry trio. The three seeded on
2026-09-03 were verified single-sourced by hand first; a registry seeded with something already
duplicated would fail on the commit that created it.

Epley formula.why: The one-rep-max estimate, read by nine call sites across four modules. A second copy is how the estimate starts disagreeing with itself between the runner and My Progress. See bugs/2026-09-03-estimate1rm-inflates-a-single-by-3-percent -- if that judgement changes, it must change in exactly one place.

Supabase client construction.why: TWO clients means two auth sessions in one tab: one refreshes its token, the other does not, and requests start failing on whichever half of the app holds the stale one. There is one client, built in app-core, and everything else uses `db`.

Metres per mile.why: A unit constant. The related weight constants are ALREADY duplicated in two different forms (_WEIGHT_KG_TO_LB = 2.2046226218 in app-core.js:182 and lbs: v => v * 0.45359237 in app-progress.js:431), which is the Phase 3 consolidation -- this pins the one that is still clean before it goes the same way.
